bull.b: The private placement and attached warrants provide multi-year optionality and explicitly fund a pivot to neoadjuvant BOT+BAL with a global Phase 3 ROBBIN trial. This concentrates resources on a larger, earlier-stage market and increases the chance of achieving high-impact clinical milestones.

A sharp decline in reported debt versus 2025 materially lowers interest and refinancing pressure, improving financial flexibility. Reduced leverage supports ongoing R&D financing and partnership negotiations, making it easier to fund trials without immediate costly restructurings.

Re-election of directors, approval of compensation and equity initiatives, and auditor ratification maintain leadership continuity and governance stability. That stability helps execution of long-duration programs and supports retention of scientific and executive teams through key clinical inflection points.

bear.b: Cumulative negative equity reflects multi-year losses and a thin capital base, limiting borrowing capacity and increasing the likelihood of future equity dilutions. Over time this erodes financial flexibility and can worsen financing terms for critical R&D and trial execution.

Large, persistent operating and free cash outflows mean the company must regularly access external capital to sustain operations and trials. Even with improved burn, ongoing negative cash flow creates refinancing risk and potential dilution that can distract management and delay strategic investments.

A single-period profit follows multi-year losses and lumpy collaboration revenue, so earnings may not persist. Reliance on milestone and license timing produces volatile results, complicating long-term planning and making current profitability a potentially transient outcome.
